attribution.note: Zitron's own claim about an internal document he says he reviewed. The quoted guidance text is the document's wording, but asserting what Microsoft instructs is his claim.

semantics.note: Faithfully states the alleged managerial instruction. 'It' refers to Copilot in context. The MRI tool detail is dropped but doesn't change the commitment.

contract.note: The evaluator chose the Jul–Sep 2024 window because the guidance is undated, which is reasonable. Reading 'instructing' as endorsed guidance rather than compulsion matches ordinary usage. The source requirements fairly exclude repetitions of Zitron's own account.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no evidence items. Nothing authenticates the alleged guidance, and nothing shows Microsoft confirmed or specifically denied it. The speaker's account cannot prove itself. The evidence available does not settle the claim either way.

attribution.note: Zitron's own stated belief in his newsletter.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the 'fairly confident' hedge and the basis he cited. The referent of 'this is the case' is ambiguous but is reasonably read as comments and tests. 'Fairly confident' is graded, moderate confidence, so the claim is not scored.

contract.note: The contract applies a plain reading and literal confinement ('just') to hedged language. Policy reserves plain-reading scoring for firm language. It is also unclear whether 'just' means strict confinement or is shorthand for mostly routine work.

evidence.note: Google Research post dated within the target period. It reports AI-authored functional code changes landed in a Google Ads ID migration, which goes beyond comments and tests. It is a company disclosure about one workstream, and it doesn't change the unscored outcome.

reviews.rationale: 'Fairly confident' expresses graded, moderate confidence, which policy does not score. The question-and-answer framing also leaves the referent ambiguous. Google's July 2024 disclosure would cut against a literal 'just comments and tests' reading, but the claim is not scored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own forecast in his newsletter.

semantics.note: 'Will collapse' is firm forecast language. 'These ugly messes' plausibly refers to the large automating companies, since 'their entire infrastructure' follows. It could also mean the codebases. The horizon 'at some point' is preserved as open.

contract.note: Reading collapse as a major or sustained breakdown, with the stated causal mechanism, is an ordinary reading. The company class and severity are not defined, so the result depends on interpretation. Correctly, continued operation cannot disprove an open-ended forecast.

evidence.note: Google incident report on a 49-minute outage in Sept 2025, caused by a software-update bug and rolled back. It does not attribute the outage to AI-generated code and is not a collapse.

Alphabet Q4 2025 earnings transcript (Feb 2026), published before the evaluation date. It says about half of Google's code is written by agents and reviewed by engineers. This is a company disclosure and says nothing about a collapse.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. No dated, verified collapse caused by defective automated infrastructure appears in the evidence, so the early-resolution rule is not met. Under an open horizon, the absence of the event so far is not failure.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his newsletter.

semantics.note: Faithfully limited to class declarations, his only example. 'Minimal' is an unquantified judgment.

contract.note: Reading the claim as about functional output for routine class declarations follows from his 'outcome is the same' line. That is a fair, ordinary reading. The time window is evaluator-selected but harmless.

evidence.note: Microsoft Learn documentation of the Visual Studio C++ class snippet, dated 2025. It covers only the IDE side of the comparison and has no matched AI output, so it cannot settle the claim.

reviews.rationale: No matched comparison of class declarations from AI tools and conventional IDE tools in the target period was found. The only item documents the IDE template side. The evidence available neither supports nor contradicts the claim.
